body: For RR, we could likely get around this as we already perform this check earlier in the pipeline. However the problem would still exist for other cases

[Docs](https://quarkus.io/guides/security-built-in-authentication#proactive-authentication) says that *authentication process will only be run when an identity is requested, either because there are security rules*, that tells me that authentication for the endpoints with @RolesAllowed should be effectively always proactive (only in sense the behavior of such annotated methods should match no matter of true/false). `quarkus-extensions-security` module is aware of `javax.annotation.security.RolesAllowed` existence, thus it should be able to differentiate if the endpoint is annotated.

```
quarkus.http.auth.proactive=true
curl -v http://localhost:8080/api/admin -> 401
curl -v http://localhost:8080/api/admin -u admin:admin -> 200 admin

quarkus.http.auth.proactive=false
curl -v http://localhost:8080/api/admin -> 401
curl -v http://localhost:8080/api/admin -u admin:admin -> 500
```

The exception is thrown as `io.quarkus.security.runtime.SecurityIdentityAssociation#getIdentity` uses `deferredIdentity` when `proactive=false` and `identity` when `proactive=true` (so it don't have to block).  `io.quarkus.vertx.http.runtime.security.HttpSecurityRecorder#authenticationMechanismHandler` got passed `proactiveAuthentication` and if it's true, it authenticates user (thus potentially get identity). In `io.vertx.ext.web.RoutingContext` is available the path and params etc. So at the very least it should be possible to active auth in RR in a same fashion for the endpoint annotated with @RolesAllowed (I don't say it's the most effective way, just an option...). Would it make sense to always resolve identity when we known there is `SecurityCheck` registered for `@RolesAllowed`? Like in the reproducer for `public java.lang.String org.acme.elytron.security.jpa.AdminResource.adminResource()`?

 I'll check over the weekended whether this conclusion makes any sense and if so, try to fix it.

issue.title: Resolve Sec. Identity in RESTEasy Reactive when Proactive Auth disabled
issue.body:
f ix #23547 for RESTEasy Reactive cases (e.g. the issue reproducer)

Disabling proactive authentication [makes accessing the `SecurityIdentity` the blocking operation](https://quarkus.io/guides/security-built-in-authentication#proactive-authentication). In RR security checks for these of standard security annotations that requires access to `SecurityIdentity` (e.g. `@RollesAllowed`) are [further up the handler chain](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/19598) then same checks run by Quarkus Security Runtime (`io.quarkus.security.deployment.SecurityProcessor#registerSecurityInterceptors`). Checks run in RR access SecurityIndentity by `getDeferredIdentity` (non-blocking), however in Quarkus Security the checks are using `getIdentity`. That leads to `BlockingOperationNotAllowedException` when running synchronously on IO thread. The `quarkus-security-runtime-spi` does not allow to disable security checks (that make sense from security point of view, but f.e `io.quarkus.security.runtime.interceptor.check.RolesAllowedCheck` is always run twice if successful), but as checks in RR always run first, this PR sets the identity there to make it available later in the chain.

body: I don't think that it's possible to impl. the issue "Expected behavior" (fail with more informative message) for all usages of vertx-http - the ex. message is very clear in information Quarkus Security has, vertx-http has no knowledge of link between route and RBAC annotated endpoint. It must be done on the level where route is already linked with REST endpoint/CDI bean method. F.e. in RR.

issue.title: Resolve Sec. Identity in Reactive routes when Proactive Auth disabled
issue.body:
Fix #23547 for Reactive routes (follow up to #26457)

When proactive authentication was disabled and `@RollesAllowed`, `@Authenticated`, or `@DenyAll` was used in non-blocking (e.g. method wasn't annotated with `@Blocking`) context and route method response type was not uni/multi/completionstage, then `BlockingOperationNotAllowedException` was thrown as `SecurityConstrainer` called a blocking operation `getIdentity` on IO thread. Such a cases are detected now in a build time and later the handler that triggers authentication is added right before body handler (if not authenticated already).

issue.title: RESTEasy Reactive - Perform eager security checks for JaxRS security
issue.body:
fix: #26553

Same issue as with #23547, security checks with disabled proactive security on the IO thread performed by `SecurityConstrainer` leads to an exception as identity is accessed in a synchronous manner. Now these checks are performed eagerly in RR so by the time checks are performed by `SecurityConstrainer`, user is already authenticated - same situation as with RBAC annotations.

issue.title: Apply additional JAX-RS security only for endpoints and not all resource methods
issue.body:
fixes: #28791

When using JAX-RS security configuration properties `quarkus.security.jaxrs.deny-unannotated-endpoints` and `quarkus.security.jaxrs.default-roles-allowed` all resource methods that can be intercepted (endpoints or not) are secured by security interceptors (e.g. `DenyAllInterceptor` and `RolesAllowedInterceptor`). This leads to unexpected behavior when non-endpoints are invoked in a fashion that can be intercepted, one example - add `@ServerExceptionMapper` to a resource (methods annotated with this annotation also expects to be in resource, see its Javadoc), this mapper method will be secured (and if it handles Unauthorized, it should lead to circular reference).

This PR secures endpoints rather than classes. To do that in RR, I had to extract logic behind endpoint selection (to keep the logic in one place).

body: @michalvavrik Looks like it is resolved as well ?

yeah @sberyozkin, Martin speaks about resource method and that's resolved.

There is related problem with bean methods annotated with RBAC running on IO thread that returns something in a synchronous manner (e.g. you have non-blocking resource method that call service method like String getMe() and getMe is annotated with @RolesAllowed), but that's really difficult to fix if authentication didn't happen further up in the chain. In order to get identity, you would have to switch thread or rewrite the way intercepted methods are invoked.

Maybe we could simply document it, WDYT @sberyozkin ?

issue.title: Document RBAC used on CDI beans and IO thread when method returns "something" in a synchronous manner
issue.body:
closes: #23547 (together with #26529)

Document known issue when RBAC annotation is used on CDI beans and method that is invoked from IO thread return "something" in a synchronous manner. While it works in certain situations (if authentication happen further up the stream and current identity association has been intentionally set; in short, that's rare), it seems dodgy and we should warn users. See also https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/23547#issuecomment-1311871210.
